To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the apelin gene promoter is regulated transcriptionally by USF, and that the expression of apelin is increased during pregnancy and lactating in rat breast.

1) the rat apelin gene promoter is a TATA‐less gene; 2) the rat and human 5'‐flanking sequences of the apelin genes contain putative USF‐binding sites and USF‐1 and ‐2 are capable of stimulating basal and inducibly regulated apelin gene transcription; and 3) USF is recruited and binds to the apelin gene promoter in breast during lactation.

(a) USF is a key transcription factor that regulates apelin transcription in breast; (b) USF‐1 and ‐2 bind to the apelin core promoter; (c) apelin is expressed at higher levels during pregnancy and lactational periods, when USF binding to its promoter is increased; and (d) USF is recruited in vivo to the apelin gene promoter in lactating breast.
